name: Point Nepean
intro: Point Nepean is the Peninsula at its most exposed and historically strange: quarantine station buildings facing the bay, old gun emplacements buried in coastal scrub, and walking tracks that keep revealing a new view across Port Phillip Heads just when you think the drama has peaked. It is less a single attraction than a whole day of edges  -  military ruins, tea-tree, pale water, and the sense that Melbourne has fallen clean away behind you. Go early, wear proper shoes, and give yourself time to keep stopping at the lookouts.
factualLede: Point Nepean is the western tip of the Mornington Peninsula, 100 km from Melbourne, a national park covering the historic quarantine station, fortifications and the entry to Port Phillip Bay.

heroImage.alt: Looking out towards the waves near Cheviot Hill at Point Nepean

tldr: Point Nepean National Park is the Peninsula's most dramatic walk - quarantine station ruins, gun emplacements, and views across Port Phillip Heads at the continent's edge.
Best for: walkers; history enthusiasts; anyone who wants to understand the Peninsula beyond its wine and beach reputation.
Signature experience: the Forts Walk from the visitor centre to Fort Nepean, timed to arrive at the headland in the last two hours of light.
Entry is free; a shuttle runs along the old army road to the fort precinct.
Full day; go early and stay late.
notFor: anyone wanting a casual quick stop
signature: The end of the Peninsula, where military ruins and ocean light do the same job of making Melbourne feel very far away.
skip: Driving in and rushing the forts - Point Nepean only works if you give it time and walk it properly.
bestDay: Start at the Quarantine Station, walk or shuttle to the forts, stay out on the headland until late light.
insiderNote: Most people turn back too early; the final stretch to Fort Nepean is the part that actually earns the trip.
